evals.name: multi-task-deliverables
evals.prompt: I'm wrapping up a small demo project before tomorrow. In the scratch project at <SCRATCH_DIR>, I need: (1) a NOTES.md summarizing what each of config.py, math_utils.py, and string_utils.py does, (2) a CHANGELOG.md with an entry for 'v0.1.0 - initial utility release', (3) a TESTING.md listing manual checks to run before the demo, and (4) the obvious style issues fixed in string_utils.py (inconsistent quote style and missing docstrings). These four things are all pretty independent of each other. Can you just get through all of it?
evals.expected_output: All four deliverables exist and are individually correct: NOTES.md accurately describes the three source files, CHANGELOG.md has a properly formatted v0.1.0 entry, TESTING.md lists concrete manual checks relevant to the actual functions in the project, and string_utils.py has consistent quote style plus docstrings on all three functions with its behavior unchanged. The final reply to the user is one consolidated summary, not a play-by-play of each task.
expectations: NOTES.md exists in the scratch project and accurately describes what config.py, math_utils.py, and string_utils.py each do
CHANGELOG.md exists with a 'v0.1.0' entry describing an initial utility release
TESTING.md exists and lists concrete manual checks tied to the actual functions in the project (not generic boilerplate)
string_utils.py uses one consistent quote style throughout and every function has a docstring
string_utils.py's functions still behave the same as before (slugify, truncate, reverse_words logic unchanged)
The task was carried out via delegation to multiple subagents (Agent/Task tool calls), not the executor doing all four deliverables itself serially
The final message to the user is a single consolidated summary of all four deliverables, not a separate blow-by-blow narration per task

evals.name: single-trivial-fix
evals.prompt: In the scratch project at <SCRATCH_DIR>, can you fix the typo in README.md where it says 'Instalation' instead of 'Installation'?
evals.expected_output: README.md is fixed directly and quickly. Because this is one trivial, single-step task, no subagents are spawned for it - the executor just makes the edit itself.
expectations: No other content in README.md was changed unnecessarily
The fix was made directly without spawning any subagents (no Agent/Task tool calls) - a single-task fix should not trigger delegation overhead
